claims.title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
claims.summary: Germanic tribes under Arminius destroyed three Roman legions commanded by Varus, ending Roman attempts to conquer Germania east of the Rhine and securing the river as a permanent frontier.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-9-battle-of-the-teutoburg-forest, claim TL:DEU:event:9:battle-of-the-teutoburg-forest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coronation of Charlemagne
claims.summary: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans in Rome, reviving the western imperial title and binding the German lands into a renewed Christian empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-800-coronation-of-charlemagne, claim TL:DEU:event:800:coronation-of-charlemagne, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Verdun
claims.summary: Charlemagne's grandsons divided the Carolingian empire into three kingdoms. East Francia, the German-speaking eastern share, became the foundation of the future Kingdom of Germany.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-843-treaty-of-verdun, claim TL:DEU:event:843:treaty-of-verdun, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Otto I crowned emperor
claims.summary: Pope John XII crowned Otto I of East Francia emperor in Rome, uniting the German and Italian kingdoms and founding the Holy Roman Empire that would frame German political life for over 800 years.

sources.label: 962: The Establishment of the Holy Roman Empire

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-962-otto-i-crowned-emperor, claim TL:DEU:event:962:otto-i-crowned-emperor, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
claims.summary: Martin Luther issued his Ninety-five Theses against the sale of indulgences, sparking the Protestant Reformation that split Western Christianity and reshaped German society and language.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1517-luther-s-ninety-five-theses, claim TL:DEU:event:1517:luther-s-ninety-five-theses, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peace of Augsburg
claims.summary: The imperial diet established the first lasting legal coexistence of Lutheranism and Catholicism, letting each prince set his territory's religion under the principle cuius regio, eius religio.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1555-peace-of-augsburg, claim TL:DEU:event:1555:peace-of-augsburg, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Thirty Years' War and the Peace of Westphalia
claims.summary: A devastating European war fought largely in Germany ended with the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, which confirmed the autonomy of the empire's states and entrenched German fragmentation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1618-the-thirty-years-war-and-the-peace-of-westphalia, claim TL:DEU:event:1618:the-thirty-years-war-and-the-peace-of-westphalia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire
claims.summary: Under pressure from Napoleon, Emperor Francis II abdicated the imperial crown and dissolved the Holy Roman Empire, ending the medieval framework of German statehood after more than eight centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1806-dissolution-of-the-holy-roman-empire, claim TL:DEU:event:1806:dissolution-of-the-holy-roman-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Congress of Vienna and the German Confederation
claims.summary: After Napoleon's defeat, the Congress of Vienna created a loose confederation of German states dominated by Austria and Prussia, leaving national unity unfulfilled.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1815-congress-of-vienna-and-the-german-confederation, claim TL:DEU:event:1815:congress-of-vienna-and-the-german-confederation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Revolutions of 1848
claims.summary: Liberal and nationalist uprisings swept the German states, and the Frankfurt Parliament drafted a constitution for a united Germany, but the movement collapsed when the Prussian king refused its imperial crown.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1848-the-revolutions-of-1848, claim TL:DEU:event:1848:the-revolutions-of-1848, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of the German Empire
claims.summary: Following victory in the Franco-Prussian War, the German states united as the German Empire, proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles with Wilhelm I as Emperor and Bismarck as Chancellor.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1871-proclamation-of-the-german-empire, claim TL:DEU:event:1871:proclamation-of-the-german-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bismarckian empire and industrial rise
claims.summary: Under Bismarck's chancellorship the empire industrialised rapidly and introduced the world's first national social insurance, while maintaining a careful balance of power in Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1871-the-bismarckian-empire-and-industrial-rise, claim TL:DEU:event:1871:the-bismarckian-empire-and-industrial-rise, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: German colonial expansion
claims.summary: Germany acquired colonies in Africa and the Pacific, a latecomer's empire whose rule, including the genocide of the Herero and Nama in South West Africa, left a brutal legacy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1884-german-colonial-expansion, claim TL:DEU:event:1884:german-colonial-expansion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The First World War
claims.summary: Germany fought the First World War as the principal Central Power. Four years of total war devastated a generation and ended in German defeat.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1914-the-first-world-war, claim TL:DEU:event:1914:the-first-world-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abdication of Wilhelm II
claims.summary: Amid military collapse and revolution, Emperor Wilhelm II abdicated and a republic was proclaimed in Berlin; the armistice followed two days later, ending the war and the monarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1918-abdication-of-wilhelm-ii, claim TL:DEU:event:1918:abdication-of-wilhelm-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Weimar Republic and its constitution
claims.summary: Germany's first democracy adopted the Weimar Constitution in 1919, establishing a parliamentary republic that would be undermined by economic crisis and political extremism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1919-the-weimar-republic-and-its-constitution, claim TL:DEU:event:1919:the-weimar-republic-and-its-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hitler appointed chancellor
claims.summary: President Hindenburg appointed Adolf Hitler chancellor. Within months the Nazis abolished democracy and established a totalitarian one-party dictatorship.

claims.title: Invasion of Poland
claims.summary: Germany invaded Poland, igniting the Second World War in Europe and beginning six years of conquest, occupation and total war.

sources.label: The Holocaust and World War II: Key Dates

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1939-invasion-of-poland, claim TL:DEU:event:1939:invasion-of-poland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Holocaust
claims.summary: Nazi Germany carried out the systematic, state-organised murder of some six million European Jews, alongside the killing of Roma, disabled people, Soviet prisoners and other victims.

sources.label: The Holocaust and World War II: Key Dates

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1941-the-holocaust, claim TL:DEU:event:1941:the-holocaust, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Unconditional surrender
claims.summary: Germany surrendered unconditionally to the Allies, ending the Second World War in Europe and the Nazi regime amid the ruin of the country.

sources.label: The Holocaust and World War II: Key Dates

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1945-unconditional-surrender, claim TL:DEU:event:1945:unconditional-surrender, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the two German states
claims.summary: The Basic Law established the Federal Republic of Germany in the west on 23 May 1949; the German Democratic Republic was founded in the Soviet zone on 7 October 1949, formalising the country's division.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1949-founding-of-the-two-german-states, claim TL:DEU:event:1949:founding-of-the-two-german-states, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Construction of the Berlin Wall
claims.summary: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall to stop its citizens fleeing west, creating the most potent symbol of the Cold War division of Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1961-construction-of-the-berlin-wall, claim TL:DEU:event:1961:construction-of-the-berlin-wall, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
claims.summary: Amid mass protests and the collapse of communist rule across Eastern Europe, the Berlin Wall was opened, ending the division of Berlin and clearing the path to reunification.

sources.label: Day of German Unity: Facts and History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Germany: From the forests beyond the Rhine to the heart of a united Europe.", terralore.co/country/DEU/chronicle#ev-1989-fall-of-the-berlin-wall, claim TL:DEU:event:1989:fall-of-the-berlin-wall, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: German reunification
claims.summary: The German Democratic Republic acceded to the Federal Republic, reuniting Germany as a single democratic state, now commemorated annually as the Day of German Unity.

sources.label: Day of German Unity: Facts and History
